description: Claim 1 is an office visit with lab tests and is correct. Claim 2 has a single line, an X-ray of the chest with the $25 imaging copay, but the claim's member-share total is $10.00 higher than that line. A careful reviewer should add up the line, see that the printed total does not match it, and conclude the member owes the line amount, not the larger total.

sources.what: The EOB must report billed, approved, plan-paid and member amounts per item and as cumulative totals, so a claim's printed totals must add up its lines
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.111(k)(1) and (k)(2), Disclosure requirements (Part C explanation of benefits: amounts per item and year-to-date totals), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.111

sources.what: A Medicare Advantage plan mails an EOB each month you visit a provider, summarizing your claims and costs
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Checking the status of a claim, https://www.medicare.gov/providers-services/claims-appeals-complaints/claims/check-status

sources.what: Review each statement you get for accuracy
